problems: 'fixed-in-release': the thread only has the maintainer's intent to revert the API change, no release or merged fix
cause_fixed: pyOCD 0.35.0 changed the DPConnector constructor signature, breaking callers (such as NXP SPSDK) that passed only the probe.
fix_fixed: Pass the debug port explicitly as the second argument (DPConnector(probe, probe.session.board.target.dp)), as done on the SPSDK side; the maintainer said he would find a way to revert the API change.

problems: versions '0.35' not named in the thread (only pack NXP.MIMXRT685S_DFP 16.0.0)

cause_fixed: The NXP pack uses C-style 'U' suffixes on integer literals in a debug sequence, which pyOCD's parser rejected. After that, DebugPortStart was assigned to the named core cm33; pyOCD did not support core-specific DebugPort* sequences, so the debug unlock sequence did not run and the CM33 access port stayed disabled.
fix_fixed: Parser fix in pull request #1548 (installable from the branch). For the second problem remove Pname="cm33" from the DebugPortStart sequence in the pdsc and pass the expanded pack directory to --pack, until core-specific port sequences are supported. Use the .FLM extracted from the pack, not NXP's .cfx.

fix_fixed: No fix in the thread. Maintainer and reporter agreed that _get_string() should return bytes and only text-mode files be encoded/decoded, and that target libraries (picolibc) should open files in binary mode by default.

problems: 'use a CMSIS-DAP firmware on the Pico' is not suggested in the thread; the picoprobe author reports signal-integrity problems with a Pico as CMSIS-DAP too
cause_fixed: Probable signal-integrity trouble; the picoprobe code speeds up SWD by assuming positive acknowledgements from the target, and the firmware leaves the pins at a fast slew rate.
fix_fixed: Lower the SWD clock (-f 400000) and replug the probe when problems show; -Opicoprobe.safeswd=True disables the assumed acknowledgements (much slower).

problems: the cause is stated as fact; the maintainer only says packets look out of order or mixed up and that the VM may work because of lower USB performance
option given without a value; the working form in the thread is -Ocmsis_dap.limit_packets=1
cause_fixed: Command packets appear to get out of order, dropped or mixed up between pyOCD on macOS and a custom CMSIS-DAP firmware (private DAPLink fork on a K22F); the maintainer suspected the Ubuntu VM worked only because of lower USB performance.
fix_fixed: Add -Ocmsis_dap.limit_packets=1 (the =True form was not accepted until change #1259); the maintainer also suggested rebasing the firmware on the current DAPLink develop branch.

problems: 'Use a vendor tool' is not in the thread
cause_fixed: The CY8CKIT-059 has KitProg (v1), which has no CMSIS-DAP mode; pyOCD supports only KitProg2 in CMSIS-DAP mode and KitProg3. PSoC 5LP devices are not really supported by pyOCD either (no CMSIS-Pack, no flash programming).
fix_fixed: No fix for this kit in pyOCD; only KitProg2 (switched to CMSIS-DAP mode with its button) or KitProg3 probes are detected.

problems: 'recover the device (reset or erase)' is not in the thread; the maintainer even doubts that connect under reset works on LPC55xx
cause_fixed: The target was not responding on SWD because the application had muxed one of the SWD pins to another function (the maintainer notes 'No ACK received' usually means low-power sleep or muxed SWD pins).
fix_fixed: Remove the application's pin configuration that reassigns the SWD pin; then flashing works.

problems: debug sequences are presented as usable; the thread says they exist only on the maintainer's feature branch, not upstream
cause_fixed: The built-in STM32L475 target had wrong addresses for the DBGMCU APB1FZR2 and APB2FZR freeze registers.
fix_fixed: Fixed by change #1193. For other STM32 parts (e.g. L496) use the CMSIS pack target and write DBGMCU registers from a user script (did_connect hook); debug sequence support was only on the maintainer's feature/debug_sequences branch.

problems: the mechanism of the 0.32.0 fix (tolerate strings, fall back to protocol 1.0.0) is only the plan discussed in the thread; the thread only says the issue is resolved in 0.32.0
cause_fixed: Some probe firmwares (Microchip EDBG, Particle DAPLink) put a vendor firmware revision in the DAP_Info field that pre-2.1 CMSIS-DAP specs loosely called firmware version but that means protocol version; pyOCD tried to parse it as numbers.
fix_fixed: Upgrade to pyOCD 0.32.0 or later, where the maintainer says this is resolved (the change discussed was to handle the parse error and default to CMSIS-DAP protocol 1.0.0 for unknown values).

problems: 'fell back to generic handling' is a mechanism the thread does not give

fix_fixed: Add a built-in target for the LPC5526 like the LPC55S28 one; the reporter did this and could then flash, erase and debug.

problems: 'Fixed in a pyOCD 0.30.x patch release' is not in the thread; the maintainer only promises a new version with the fix from PR #1128
cause_fixed: The Picoprobe probe class raised NoBackendError while enumerating probes when no libusb backend was installed, instead of just reporting no probes.

problems: 'later releases include the improved detection' and 'fixed-in-release' are not in the thread; only a maintainer branch tested by the reporter is shown
cause_fixed: pyOCD recognises HID CMSIS-DAP probes by 'CMSIS-DAP' in the product name; the WCH-Link's product string lacks it, hidapi does not report interface names, and the WCH-Link's HID interface string descriptor is broken, so the probe was ignored on macOS (Windows with pyocd 0.29.0 listed it).
fix_fixed: Install the maintainer's branch that also looks for 'CMSIS-DAP' in the hidapi device path (pip install -U git+https://github.com/flit/pyOCD@bugfix/hidapi_uid_and_if_name); the reporter confirmed the probe is then found.

problems: 'Use a pyOCD release that includes ... PR #1018 (after 0.28)': the maintainer only asked the reporter to verify that #1018 fixes it; no release or confirmation

cause_fixed: After a reset PSoC6 drops back to JTAG mode and loses DAP state, so the DAP must be fully re-initialised; since 0.28.0 dp.init() goes through the shared probe proxy, which increments its connect count and then turns the SWJ switch sequence into a no-op.
fix_fixed: Pull request #1018 is meant to fix reconnecting; the maintainer asked the reporter to verify it. The reporter's tested workaround in the PSoC6 target code re-initialises the DAP after reset (SWJ sequence, reset_did_occur on the APs, read DP IDR, clear sticky errors, power up debug).

cause_fixed: A string/bytes conversion bug in SemihostAgent._get_string() (six.ensure_str(bytes(bytearray(''))...)) raises TypeError for semihosting write requests under Python 3.

problems: the sleep diagnosis is the maintainer's likely explanation, never confirmed; 'configuration' resolution is not shown

cause_fixed: No response at all to the first SWD read; the maintainer says this most often means the MCU is asleep in a low-power mode (WFI/WFE) that disables debug, and the default Mbed build neither enables debug nor disables sleep on idle.
fix_fixed: Build with the Mbed debug profile so debug stays enabled and automatic sleep is off. --connect=under-reset did not help because the nRF52840 does not expose nRESET on a pin unless UICR.PSELRESET is programmed; otherwise try to connect while the firmware is awake or as the MCU powers on.

problems: the thread has no fix: the maintainer only says it will be fixed shortly by supporting different erase/program sizes

cause_fixed: The STM32F401RE has 128 kB sectors, so the flash algorithm and its data buffer do not fit in the available RAM; the pack sector parsing also mishandled the (start, size) tuples, causing the TypeError.
